paras.t: Denique non obstante quod per Moysen facta sunt signa hæc, quibus Ægyptus destructa est, tamen Ægyptii videntes tot supernaturalia per Moysen fieri, habuerunt eum pro viro eximio, sicut subjungitur : Fuitque Moyses vir magnus valde in terra Ægypti coram servis Pharaonis et omni populo Ægyptiorum. Nec dubium, quin et coram Hebræis. Pharao autem elatione cæcatus, ultimo dixit ad eum, Cave ne ultra videas faciem meam, etc., ut patuit in fine præcedentis capituli.
paras.en: Lastly, although these signs by which Egypt was laid waste were done through Moses, yet the Egyptians, seeing so many supernatural things done through Moses, held him to be an outstanding man, as is added: [[11:3|And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharao's servants, and of all the people|Fuitque Moyses vir magnus valde in terra Ægypti coram servis Pharaonis et omni populo]] of the Egyptians. Nor is there any doubt that he was so in the sight of the Hebrews too. But Pharao, blinded by pride, said to him at the last, [[Ex 10:28|beware thou see not my face any more|Cave ne ultra videas faciem meam]], etc., as appeared at the end of the preceding chapter.

paras.t: Et ait Pharaoni et ejus ministris, insinuando eis revelationem sibi factam a Deo : Hæc dicit Dominus : Media nocte ingre[…] Ægyptum, quod intelligitur de nocte illa secunda, in qua primogenita sunt occisa, quæ fuit post aliquot dies post hæc, ut ex sequenti capitulo elucescit. Ingressus est autem Dominus Ægyptum non per suæ deitatis motum aut mutationem, sed per justitiæ suæ effectum. Nam subditur : et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum, a primogenito Pharaonis inclusive, qui sedet in solio ejus, hoc est, jus hereditarium regnandi habet pro patre suo : vel, jam constitutus fuit in principatu a patre suo : quod tamen non videtur, quia in textu ubique Pharao iste insinuatur regnasse usque ad suam submersionem ; usque ad primogenitum ancillæ, quæ est ad molam : hoc est a supremo usque ad infimum inclusive ; et omnia primogenita jumentorum morientur, prout sequenti recitatur capitulo. Eritque clamor magnus in universa terra Ægypti, qualis nec ante fuit, nec postea futurus est. Ululabant namque, flebant, et clamitabant Ægyptii, tam ex dolore plagæ inflictæ, quam ex timore plagæ gravioris infligendæ. Verumtamen instante fine sæculi, arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione eorum quæ supervenient universo orbi, erit ubique terrarum incomparabilis dolor, timor, angustia. Moyses vero nunc loquitur de speciali Ægyptiorum calamitate atque clamore, non de universali generis humani ærumna.
paras.en: [[11:4|And he said|Et ait]] to Pharao and his ministers, making known to them the revelation given him by God: [[11:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[11:4|At midnight|Media nocte]] […] [[11:4|I will enter into Egypt|Ægyptum]] [part of a word is lost in the transcription here; below Denis reads *ingrediar Ægyptum*, "I will enter Egypt", where the Vulgate has *egrediar in Ægyptum*], which is to be understood of that later night in which the firstborn were slain, which came some days after this, as is clear from the next chapter. Now the Lord entered Egypt not by any movement or change of His Godhead, but by the effect of His justice. For it is added: [[11:5|And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die, from the firstborn of Pharao|et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum, a primogenito Pharaonis]] inclusive, [[11:5|who sitteth on his throne|qui sedet in solio ejus]], that is, who holds the hereditary right to reign after his father; or, who had already been set in the government by his father: though this does not seem so, because everywhere in the text this Pharao is implied to have reigned until he was drowned; [[11:5|even to the firstborn of the handmaid that is at the mill|usque ad primogenitum ancillæ, quæ est ad molam]]: that is, from the highest to the lowest inclusive; [[11:5|and all the firstborn of beasts|et omnia primogenita jumentorum]] shall die, as is told in the next chapter. [[11:6|And there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as neither hath been before, nor shall be hereafter|Eritque clamor magnus in universa terra Ægypti, qualis nec ante fuit, nec postea futurus est]]. For the Egyptians howled, wept and cried out, as much from the pain of the plague inflicted as from fear of a heavier plague yet to be inflicted. Yet when the end of the world is at hand, with men [[Luke 21:26|withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione eorum quæ supervenient universo orbi]], there will be everywhere on earth a pain, fear and anguish beyond compare. But Moses is speaking here of the particular calamity and cry of the Egyptians, not of the universal affliction of the human race.

paras.t: Apud omnes autem filios Israel non mutiet canis ab homine usque ad pecus : hoc est, tanta quies atque securitas erunt in Hebræis et eorum pecoribus, quod nec canis, qui ex facili latrat occasione, latratum emittet. Per quem modum loquendi designatur præcipua pax Hebræorum. Et potest hoc verbum per modum hyperbolicæ locutionis intelligi. Ut sciatis quanto miraculo dividat Dominus Ægyptios et Israel, hoc est, quam miraculose ostendat pietatem suam circa Israelitas, et rigorem justitiæ circa Ægyptios.
paras.en: [[11:7|But with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise, from man even to beast|Apud omnes autem filios Israel non mutiet canis ab homine usque ad pecus]]: that is, there shall be such quiet and security among the Hebrews and their flocks that not even a dog, which barks at the slightest occasion, shall give a bark. This manner of speaking signifies the singular peace of the Hebrews. And this saying can also be understood as a hyperbole. [[11:7|that you may know how wonderful a difference the Lord maketh between the Egyptians and Israel|Ut sciatis quanto miraculo dividat Dominus Ægyptios et Israel]], that is, how miraculously He shows His loving kindness towards the Israelites and the rigour of His justice towards the Egyptians.

paras.t: Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me. Hoc Moyses dixit de se ipso : nam subditur, et adorabunt me adoratione duliæ, id est rogabunt. Unde aliqui habent, Orabunt. Dicentes : Egredere tu et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi, hoc est tota plebs Israelitica : Post hæc egrediemur Ægyptum. Vel sensus est, quod servi Pharaonis descendentes in terram Gessen, adorabunt Deum Israel, quem ex tantis prodigiis aliqualiter cognoverunt, ut ipse Dominus Deus Hebræorum cum populo suo ab Ægypto discederet, ne amplius plagaret Ægyptios. Moyses quippe post hæc rediit ad terram Gessen, et eo exsistente ibidem, primogenita sunt percussa. Quo facto, servi Pharaonis venerunt illuc, ut infra habetur.
paras.en: [[11:8|And all these thy servants shall come down to me|Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me]]. Moses said this of himself: for it is added, [[11:8|and shall worship me|et adorabunt me]] with the worship of dulia [that is, the honour paid to a creature, as distinct from latria, the worship due to God alone], that is, they shall entreat me. Hence some read *Orabunt*, "they shall pray". [[11:8|saying: Go forth thou, and all the people that is under thee|Dicentes : Egredere tu et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi]], that is, the whole people of Israel: [[11:8|after that we will go out|Post hæc egrediemur]] of Egypt. Or the sense is that Pharao's servants, coming down into the land of Gessen, will worship the God of Israel, whom they had come to know in some measure from such great wonders, praying that the Lord God of the Hebrews would Himself depart from Egypt with His people, so as to plague the Egyptians no more. For after this Moses went back to the land of Gessen, and while he was there the firstborn were struck. When this was done, Pharao's servants came there, as is told below.

paras.t: Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis. Moyses quamvis esset mitissimus, tamen ex zelo justitiæ fuit multum iratus secundum rationis dictamen, tam inauditam impii regis obdurationem, ingratitudinem, rebellionem, et comminationem detestans atque admirans, imo et juste puniri saltem in vita hac cupiens. Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen : Non audiet auribus cordis eos Pharao, donec rursus tangatur, ut multa signa fiant in terra Ægypti. Quod ex Pharaonis obstinatione consecutum est, non directe causaliter, sed concomitanter. Certumque est, quod Pharao non ob hoc non audivit Moysen, quatenus signa multiplicarentur, quia non intendebat, neque optabat hoc. Porro post hæc facta est percussio primogenitorum, divisio maris Rubri, submersio Ægyptiorum. Moyses autem et Aaron fecerunt ministerialiter, non efficienter et principaliter, omnia ostenta quæ scripta sunt, coram Pharaone, hoc est præfata signa quæ fuerunt ostensione et admiratione dignissima. Nec solum fuit miranda signorum illorum productio, sed et eorum, saltem aliquorum, cessatio, ut ex præhabitis constat.
paras.en: [[11:9|And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry|Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis]]. Moses, though he was most meek[[Num 12:3||]], was yet very angry out of zeal for justice, according to the dictate of reason, abhorring and marvelling at the unheard-of hardness, ingratitude, rebellion and threatening of the wicked king, and indeed desiring that he be justly punished, at least in this life. [[11:9|But the Lord said to Moses|Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[11:9|Pharao will not hear|Non audiet]] with the ears of the heart [[11:9|you|eos]] [Denis reads *eos*, "them", where the Vulgate has *vos*, "you"] until he is struck again, [[11:9|that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt|ut multa signa fiant in terra Ægypti]]. This followed from Pharao's obstinacy not as its direct effect but as something accompanying it. And it is certain that Pharao did not refuse to hear Moses for this end, that the signs might be multiplied, for he neither intended nor desired this. Moreover, after this came the striking of the firstborn, the dividing of the Red Sea, and the drowning of the Egyptians. [[11:10|And Moses and Aaron did|Moyses autem et Aaron fecerunt]], as ministers, not as the efficient and principal cause, [[11:10|all the wonders that are written, before Pharao|omnia ostenta quæ scripta sunt, coram Pharaone]], that is, the aforesaid signs, which were most worthy to be shown and marvelled at. And not only was the bringing about of those signs to be marvelled at, but also the ceasing of them, at least of some, as is plain from what has gone before.

paras.t: Juxta intelligentiam spiritualem docemur ex isto capitulo, quod Deo resistere non est consultum, sicut et Christus locutus est Paulo : Durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare. Idcirco qui Dei sentit percussionem, protinus se emendet, ne durioribus plagis afficiatur, attendens quod scriptum est : Amove a me plagas tuas. Et causa ibidem subjicitur : A fortitudine manus tuæ ego defeci in increpationibus.
paras.en: According to the spiritual understanding, we are taught by this chapter that it is not wise to resist God, as Christ too said to Paul: [[Acts 9:5|It is hard for thee to kick against the goad|Durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare]]. Therefore whoever feels God's stroke should amend himself at once, lest he be afflicted with harder plagues, heeding what is written: [[Ps 38:11|Remove thy scourges from me|Amove a me plagas tuas]]. And the reason is given in the same place: [[Ps 38:11|The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes|A fortitudine manus tuæ ego defeci in increpationibus]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxviii, 11, 12; in the Vulgate these words begin v. 12, in the Douay-Rheims they end v. 11; *plagas*, "plagues" or "strokes", is the Douay's "scourges"].

paras.t: Quid autem per vasa aurea atque argentea Ægyptiorum, et mutuationem eorum signetur, in expositione tertii capituli patuit. Fuit autem Moyses vir magnus valde coram servis Pharaonis. Sic et quilibet nostrum studeat esse spiritualiter magnum, hoc est valde virtuosus ac sapiens, ita ut sit bonus odor Christi in omni loco, et sæcularibus exemplaris exsistat. Est itaque magnus valde, qui est profunde humilis, perfecte patiens, fractus, et sibimet mortuus, vivens ac fervens in Domino.
paras.en: What is signified by the vessels of gold and silver of the Egyptians, and by the borrowing of them, was shown in the exposition of the third chapter[[Ex 3:22||]]. [[11:3|And Moses was a very great man|Fuit autem Moyses vir magnus valde]] [[11:3|in the sight of Pharao's servants|coram servis Pharaonis]]. So too let each of us strive to be great in spirit, that is, very virtuous and wise, so that he may be the [[2 Cor 2:15|good odour of Christ|bonus odor Christi]] in every place, and a pattern to those of the world. And so he is very great who is deeply humble, perfectly patient, broken and dead to himself, living and fervent in the Lord.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Dominus : Media nocte ingrediar Ægyptum, et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum. Hoc spiritualiter agitur, dum Deus corda hominum visitat gratiose, quando adhuc sunt in profunda vitiorum caligine, perimitque in eis universa peccata mortalia, illos ad veram contritionem instigans. Tunc plane generatur incomparabilis dolor, clamorque cordis, id est interna ac fervens devotio inter eos, qui in tenebris sæculi, quasi in Ægypto, fuerunt. Contritio namque est maximus dolor, quia de malo culpæ et summi boni offensa atque amissione, oportet maxime dolere, quemadmodum et necesse est summum bonum incomparabiliter semper diligere. Qui vero sic visitantur et illustrantur a Domino, sua perpendunt peccata, et intime deflent ea.
paras.en: [[11:4|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[11:4|At midnight I will enter into Egypt|Media nocte ingrediar Ægyptum]], [[11:5|And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die|et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum]]. This is done spiritually when God visits the hearts of men with His grace while they are still in the deep darkness of vice, and slays in them all mortal sins, moving them to true contrition. Then indeed there arises a pain beyond compare, and a cry of the heart, that is, an inward and fervent devotion, among those who were in the darkness of the world as in Egypt. For contrition is the greatest pain, since for the evil of guilt, and for the offence and loss of the highest good, one must grieve most of all, just as one must always love the highest good beyond compare. Those who are thus visited and enlightened by the Lord weigh their sins and weep for them from the heart.

paras.t: Apud filios Israel non mutiet canis : id est, in cordibus contemplativorum abundabit pax pectoris, nec iræ ceterarumque passionum erit tumultus in eis, sed vita secreta, quemadmodum in Isaia Dominus protestatur : Erit opus justitiæ pax, et cultus justitiæ silentium : et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta. Et […] quanto […] ho, etc. Ex his equidem claret quantum inter carnales et spirituales, inter sæculares et vere religiosos, inter passionatos et contemplativos distet ac differat, et quam diversimode Dominus operetur in eis.
paras.en: [[11:7|with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise|Apud filios Israel non mutiet canis]]: that is, in the hearts of contemplatives peace of heart shall abound, and there shall be in them no tumult of anger or of the other passions, but a hidden life, as the Lord declares in Isaias: [[Is 32:17|the work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice quietness|opus justitiæ pax, et cultus justitiæ silentium]]: [[Is 32:18|And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]]. And […] [[11:7|how wonderful|quanto]] […], etc. [most of this lemma, from v. 7, is lost in the transcription]. From this it is clear how far the carnal and the spiritual, the worldly and the truly religious, the slaves of passion and the contemplatives, stand apart and differ, and in how different ways the Lord works in them.

paras.t: Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me, etc. Dum enim iniqui ita præveniuntur et compunguntur a Spiritu Sancto, humiliant se, atque in mentis humiliatione accedunt ad thronum gratiæ Dei, dicentes : Egredere tu. Quia ex consideratione suorum excessuum, divina visitatione se fatentur indignos, cum sancto Petro dicentes : Exi a me, quia homo peccator sum, Domine. Verumtamen non volunt relinqui a Domino, sed peculiari ejus consolatione ac præsentia suavi reputant se indignissimos esse, et quasi indecens eis apparet, quod Dominus tam misericordissime agit cum eis. Et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi, egredietur a nostra oppressione. Nempe iniqui qui justos premunt ac persequuntur, quum sic convertuntur, dimittunt justos egredi liberos, et venerantur eosdem, imo eorum obsequio indignos se arbitrantur.
paras.en: [[11:8|And all these thy servants shall come down to me|Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me]], etc. For when the wicked are thus forestalled and pricked to the heart by the Holy Ghost, they humble themselves and, in humility of mind, draw near [[Heb 4:16|to the throne of grace|ad thronum gratiæ]] of God, [[11:8|saying: Go forth thou|dicentes : Egredere tu]]. For in considering their excesses they confess themselves unworthy of God's visitation, saying with St Peter: [[Luke 5:8|Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord|Exi a me, quia homo peccator sum, Domine]]. Yet they do not wish to be left by the Lord; but they reckon themselves most unworthy of His special consolation and sweet presence, and it seems to them almost unfitting that the Lord deals so very mercifully with them. [[11:8|and all the people that is under thee|Et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi]] shall go out from our oppression. For the wicked who oppress and persecute the just, when they are thus converted, let the just go out free and revere them, and indeed think themselves unworthy to serve them.

paras.t: Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis. Sic et justi contra perversorum duritiam interdum zelo justitiæ irascuntur, et cupiunt eos in hac vita castigari a Domino, ne pereant in æternum. Verumtamen zelus hujusmodi esse debet secundum scientiam, hoc est discretione condiri, ut memor sit homo propriæ fragilitatis, nec immoderate fervescat : imo pro eorum oret salute quibus irascitur.
paras.en: [[11:9|And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry|Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis]]. So too the just are at times angered, out of zeal for justice, against the hardness of the perverse, and desire that they be chastised by the Lord in this life, lest they perish for ever. Yet zeal of this kind must be according to knowledge, that is, seasoned with discretion, so that a man is mindful of his own frailty and does not burn beyond measure: rather, let him pray for the salvation of those with whom he is angry.

13.title: Elucidatio capituli tertiidecimi: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens: Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum
13.title_en: Explanation of the thirteenth chapter: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Sanctify unto me every firstborn

paras.t: Præcedenti capitulo descripta est percussio primogenitorum Ægypti : nunc recitatur quod ex illa percussione sit consecutum. Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens : Sanctifica mihi, id est, meo cultui, seu honorationi deputa et applica, omne primogenitum, quod aperit vulvam in filiis Israel : hoc est omne primitivum inter filios Israel, seu Israelitarum, quod primo de matre sua egreditur, etiamsi post illud alter nullus ex eadem matre nascatur. Sicque primogenitum non distinguitur nunc contra unigenitum, sed contra secundogenitum, ac deinceps. Tam de hominibus quam de jumentis, id est tam primogenita hominum, quam primogenita brutorum. Mea enim sunt omnia : hoc est, universa primogenita sunt specialiter mea, quoniam jubeo ea mihi offerri, aut meo cultui applicari, seu ad meum honorem aliquid fieri de eisdem, prout infra in isto habetur capitulo. Vel sic : Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen : Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum, etc., id est, præcipe mihi sanctificari, seu meo cultui aut honorificentiæ deputari omne primogenitum. Nam quamvis aliqua primogenita redimebantur, et aliqua offerri non poterant, ut primogenita canum, quæ interficiebantur ; aliquid tamen fiebat de eis seu circa ea, ad Dei honorem in commemorationem potentiæ atque justitiæ ejus, quas in percussione primogenitorum Ægypti ostendit. Sicque primogenita diversimode sanctificabantur Deo, ut infra magis dicetur. Istud quoque intelligitur totum de primogenitis masculis. De omni etenim fructu primitiva seu potiora Deo sunt offerenda, et quoniam sola primitiva masculini sexus percusserat in Ægypto.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter the slaying of the firstborn of Egypt was described; now is told what followed from that slaying. [[13:1|And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying|Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens]]: [[13:2|Sanctify unto me|Sanctifica mihi]], that is, set apart and apply to my worship or honour, [[13:2|every firstborn that openeth the womb among the children of Israel|omne primogenitum, quod aperit vulvam in filiis Israel]]: that is, every first-born among the children of Israel, or of the Israelites, that comes forth first from its mother, even if no other is born of the same mother after it. And so *firstborn* is here contrasted not with *only-begotten* but with *second-born*, and so on. [[13:2|as well of men as of beasts|Tam de hominibus quam de jumentis]], that is, both the firstborn of men and the firstborn of brute beasts. [[13:2|for they are all mine|Mea enim sunt omnia]]: that is, all the firstborn are mine in a special way, since I command that they be offered to me, or applied to my worship, or that something be done with them for my honour, as is set down further on in this chapter. Or thus: [[13:1|And the Lord spoke to Moses|Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[13:2|Sanctify unto me every firstborn|Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum]], etc., that is, command that every firstborn be sanctified to me, or set apart for my worship or honour. For although some firstborn were redeemed, and some could not be offered, such as the firstborn of dogs, which were killed, yet something was done with them or about them for the honour of God, in remembrance of his power and justice, which he showed in slaying the firstborn of Egypt[[Ex 12:29||]]. And so the firstborn were sanctified to God in different ways, as will be said more fully below. All this, too, is to be understood of the male firstborn: for of every fruit the first or the best is to be offered to God, and he had struck only the firstborn of the male sex in Egypt.

paras.t: Et ait Moyses ad populum Hebræorum : Mementote diei hujus in qua egressi estis de Ægypto, quæ fuit dies quintadecima mensis primi apud eos, scilicet Aprilis aut Martii, sicut in præcedentis capituli expositione præhabitum est ; et de domo servitutis, hoc est de ipso regno Ægypti, in quo tanquam in loco et mansione durissimæ servitutis estis morati. Vel, De domo servitutis, hoc est de domibus habitationum vestrarum, quas habuistis in terra Gessen, in quibus domibus habitastis, ut servi Ægyptiorum : quoniam in manu forti, hoc est per magna signa et in fortitudine sua omnipotente, eduxit vos Dominus de loco isto. Mementote, inquam, hujus diei tam vos quam posteri vestri : ut non comedatis fermentatum, id est panem, in quo fermentum admixtum est, septem diebus quibus durat paschalis festivitas. Circa hoc Lyra allegat Rabbi Salomonem, dicentem : Præceptum non obligabat ad comedendum azyma, nisi primo die quando comedebatur agnus paschalis ; ceteris diebus sufficiebat abstinere a fermento et fermentato. Cui dicto obviare videtur, quod præcedenti capitulo a Deo jubetur, Septem diebus azyma comedetis. Circa quod dicit glossa interlinearis : Prima dies dicitur Pascha, reliqui dicuntur dies azymorum, quia videlicet azymis panibus in eis vesci oportuit.
paras.en: [[13:3|And Moses said to the people|Et ait Moyses ad populum]] of the Hebrews: [[13:3|Remember this day in which you came forth out of Egypt|Mementote diei hujus in qua egressi estis de Ægypto]], which was the fifteenth day of their first month, namely of April or March, as was said before in the exposition of the preceding chapter; [[13:3|and out of the house of bondage|et de domo servitutis]], that is, out of the kingdom of Egypt itself, in which you dwelt as in a place and abode of the harshest bondage. Or, [[13:3|out of the house of bondage|De domo servitutis]], that is, out of the houses you lived in, which you had in the land of Gessen, in which houses you dwelt as slaves of the Egyptians: [[13:3|for with a strong hand|quoniam in manu forti]], that is, by great signs and in his almighty strength, [[13:3|hath the Lord brought you forth out of this place|eduxit vos Dominus de loco isto]]. Remember, I say, this day, both you and your posterity: [[13:3|that you eat no leavened|ut non comedatis fermentatum]], that is, bread in which leaven has been mixed, for the seven days that the paschal feast lasts. On this Lyra cites Rabbi Salomon, who says: The precept did not bind them to eat unleavened bread except on the first day, when the paschal lamb was eaten; on the other days it was enough to abstain from leaven and from what was leavened. This saying seems to be contradicted by God's command in the preceding chapter: [[Ex 12:15|Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread|Septem diebus azyma comedetis]]. On which the interlinear Gloss says: The first day is called the Pasch, the rest are called the days of the unleavened bread, because on them, that is, they had to eat unleavened loaves.

paras.t: Hodie egredimini de Ægypto mense novarum frugum, quæ illo in mense habentur in territoriis illis. In quo etiam mense fiebat de primitiis fructuum novorum oblatio, estque tempus illud ad ambulandum satis conveniens.
paras.en: [[13:4|This day you go forth|Hodie egredimini]] out of Egypt [[13:4|in the month of new corn|mense novarum frugum]], which is had in that month in those regions. In that month, too, the offering of the first-fruits of the new crops was made; and that season is well suited for travelling.

paras.t: Quumque introduxerit te Dominus, si non demerueris introduci, vel te in posteris tuis, seu posteros tuos pro te, in terram Chananæi et Hethæi, etc., quam juravit patribus tuis, id est, Abrahæ, Isaac et Jacob cum juramento promisit dare posteritati eorum, ut daret tibi terram fluentem lacte et melle, id est in victualibus abundantem, observabis hunc morem sacrorum mense isto, id est, sacros dies paschales et sacrificia eorumdem celebrabis juxta ritum præfatum. Septem diebus vesceris azymis : per quod patet veritas verbi contra Rabbi Salomonem inducti ; et in die septimo erit solennitas Domini, id est, dies septima festi paschalis, erit solennis sicut et prima, ut capitulo patuit præcedenti. Azyma comedetis septem diebus. Non apparebit apud te aliquid fermentatum, nec in cunctis finibus tuis.
paras.en: [[13:5|And when the Lord shall have brought thee|Quumque introduxerit te Dominus]], if thou hast not deserved not to be brought in, or thee in thy posterity, that is, thy posterity in thy stead, [[13:5|into the land of the Chanaanite, and the Hethite|in terram Chananæi et Hethæi]], etc., [[13:5|which he swore to thy fathers|quam juravit patribus tuis]], that is, which he promised with an oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give to their posterity, [[13:5|that he would give thee|ut daret tibi]] [[13:5|a land that floweth with milk and honey|terram fluentem lacte et melle]], that is, abounding in food, [[13:5|thou shalt celebrate this manner of sacred rites in this month|observabis hunc morem sacrorum mense isto]] [Denis reads *observabis*, "thou shalt observe", for the Vulgate's *celebrabis*], that is, thou shalt celebrate the holy paschal days and their sacrifices according to the rite set out above. [[13:6|Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread|Septem diebus vesceris azymis]]: by which the truth of the saying brought against Rabbi Salomon is plain; [[13:6|and on the seventh day shall be the solemnity of the Lord|et in die septimo erit solennitas Domini]], that is, the seventh day of the paschal feast shall be solemn like the first, as appeared in the preceding chapter. [[13:7|Unleavened bread shall you eat seven days|Azyma comedetis septem diebus]]. [[13:7|there shall not be seen any thing leavened with thee, nor in all thy coasts|Non apparebit apud te aliquid fermentatum, nec in cunctis finibus tuis]].

paras.t: Narrabisque filio tuo in die illo, dicens, id est, domesticis tuis, et soboli atque discipulis causam observantiarum istarum exponens, dicendo : Hoc est quod fecit mihi Dominus quando egressus sum de Ægypto : id est, celebritas ista paschalis commemorat et designat beneficia mihi seu patribus meis desuper præstita, quando exivi Ægyptum in propria persona, vel in patribus meis, in quorum lumbis tunc eram secundum rationem seminalem et carnis massam. Et erit quasi signum in manu tua, et quasi monumentum ante oculos tuos, id est, tam incessabiliter recordaberis horum, ac si esset aliquod corporale indicium in manu tua pro recordatione ligatum, vel coram oculis tuis appensum. Porro Judæi, ut fertur, occasione horum verborum scribunt istud in schedula, quam ligant in manu sinistra sive ad brachium, et aliam schedulam eadem continentem ligant ad caput. Et ut lex Domini semper sit in ore tuo, id est, in omni tempore opportuno paratus sis legem hanc Domini confiteri et filios tuos docere. In manu enim forti eduxit te Dominus de Ægypto. Custodies hujuscemodi cultum statuto tempore a diebus in dies : hoc est, observantiam hanc paschalem omni anno servabis mense primo, sicut præfixum est, a prima die hujus festi usque ad septimum diem.
paras.en: [[13:8|And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying|Narrabisque filio tuo in die illo, dicens]], that is, explaining to those of thy household, and to thy offspring and disciples, the reason for these observances, by saying: [[13:8|This is what the Lord did to me when I came forth out of Egypt|Hoc est quod fecit mihi Dominus quando egressus sum de Ægypto]]: that is, this paschal feast commemorates and signifies the benefits bestowed from on high on me, or on my fathers, when I went out of Egypt in my own person, or in my fathers, in whose loins I then was by seminal reason and the mass of the flesh [that is, as contained in the seed and the bodily stock of his forefathers]. [[13:9|And it shall be as a sign in thy hand, and as a memorial before thy eyes|Et erit quasi signum in manu tua, et quasi monumentum ante oculos tuos]], that is, thou shalt remember these things as unceasingly as if some bodily token were tied on thy hand as a reminder, or hung before thy eyes. Now the Jews, it is said, taking occasion from these words, write this on a slip of parchment which they tie on the left hand or on the arm, and they tie another slip containing the same to the head. [[13:9|and that the law of the Lord be always in thy mouth|Et ut lex Domini semper sit in ore tuo]], that is, that at every fitting time thou be ready to confess this law of the Lord and to teach it to thy sons. [[13:9|for with a strong hand the Lord hath brought thee out of the land of Egypt|In manu enim forti eduxit te Dominus de Ægypto]]. [[13:10|Thou shalt keep this observance at the set time from days to days|Custodies hujuscemodi cultum statuto tempore a diebus in dies]]: that is, thou shalt keep this paschal observance every year in the first month, as has been laid down, from the first day of this feast to the seventh day.

paras.t: Quumque introduxerit te Dominus in terram Chananæi, sicut juravit tibi et patribus tuis, et dederit tibi eam : per quam designantur terræ omnium gentium seu decem nationum, quarum terras Deus promisit Hebræis : separabis omne quod aperit vulvam, omne scilicet primogenitum, Domino, id est, ab aliis fœtibus discernes illud, tanquam ad Deum specialiter pertinens, et quod primogenitum est in pecoribus tuis. Quidquid habueris masculini sexus, consecrabis Domino, id est, primogenita masculina Deo repones, offeres, et speciale aliquid circa illud facies ad Dei honorem. Primogeniti quippe Levitarum Deo præcipue offerebantur et consecrabantur lege collata, quia in templo Domino servierunt. Primogeniti aliarum tribuum offerebantur ; et oblati, mox redimebantur quinque siclis, ita quod de cetero non erant obligati esse ministri in cultu templi. Ideo sanctificatio et consecratio horum non fuit ita perfecta et propria, ut sanctificatio et consecratio Levitarum. Primogenita demum animalium mundorum immolaticiorum offerebantur, sacerdotumque erant. Primogenita vero animalium immundorum, quæ offerri in sacrificium non valebant, vel commutabantur, ita quod aliud animal mundum aptum immolari offerebatur pro primogenito tali, sicut subjungitur. Primogenitum asini mutabis ove : vel occidebantur, propter quod subditur, Quod si non redemeris, interficies, id est, primogenitum quod non redimebatur nec mutabatur, mox occidebatur ad Dei honorem : quia Deus hoc jussit, ne aliis usibus deputaretur, quod ipse voluit esse suum, pro memoriali quod primogenita Ægyptiorum necavit, et primogenita Israelitarum de manu percussoris salvavit. Sic ergo primogenita universorum Domino consecrabantur aliquo modo, quia aut offerebantur, aut commutabantur. Et id quod offerebatur pro eis, seu pretium pro quo vendebantur, erat sacerdotum ad sustentationem eorum : aut occidebantur. Omne autem primogenitum hominis de filiis […] id est, primogenita in […]tet filios Hebræorum, pretio (scilicet quinque siclis) redimentur, ut dictum est, demptis tamen primogenitis Levitarum.
paras.en: [[13:11|And when the Lord shall have brought thee into the land of the Chanaanite|Quumque introduxerit te Dominus in terram Chananæi]], by which are meant the lands of all the nations, that is, of the ten nations whose lands God promised to the Hebrews, [[13:11|as he swore to thee and thy fathers, and shall give it thee|sicut juravit tibi et patribus tuis, et dederit tibi eam]]: [[13:12|Thou shalt set apart all that openeth the womb|separabis omne quod aperit vulvam]], that is, every firstborn, [[13:12|for the Lord|Domino]], that is, thou shalt distinguish it from the other young as belonging to God in a special way, [[13:12|and all that is first brought forth of thy cattle|et quod primogenitum est in pecoribus tuis]]. [[13:12|whatsoever thou shalt have of the male sex, thou shalt consecrate to the Lord|Quidquid habueris masculini sexus, consecrabis Domino]], that is, thou shalt set apart the male firstborn for God, offer them, and do something special about them for God's honour. For the firstborn of the Levites, once the Law was given, were offered and consecrated to God in a particular way, because they served the Lord in the temple. The firstborn of the other tribes were offered, and once offered were at once redeemed for five sicles, so that thereafter they were not bound to be ministers in the worship of the temple. Therefore the sanctification and consecration of these was not so perfect and proper as the sanctification and consecration of the Levites. The firstborn of clean animals fit for sacrifice were offered, and belonged to the priests. But the firstborn of unclean animals, which could not be offered in sacrifice, were either exchanged, so that another clean animal fit to be sacrificed was offered in place of such a firstborn, as is added: [[13:13|The firstborn of an ass thou shalt change for a sheep|Primogenitum asini mutabis ove]]; or they were killed, for which reason it is added: [[13:13|and if thou do not redeem it, thou shalt kill it|Quod si non redemeris, interficies]], that is, a firstborn that was neither redeemed nor exchanged was at once killed for the honour of God: for God commanded this, so that what he willed to be his own should not be given over to other uses, as a memorial that he slew the firstborn of the Egyptians and saved the firstborn of the Israelites from the hand of the destroyer. So, then, the firstborn of all were in some way consecrated to the Lord, for they were either offered or exchanged, and what was offered for them, or the price for which they were sold, belonged to the priests for their support; or else they were killed. [[13:13|And every firstborn of men|Omne autem primogenitum hominis de filiis]] […] that is, the firstborn among […] the sons of the Hebrews shall be redeemed with a price (namely five sicles), as has been said, except, however, the firstborn of the Levites.

paras.t: Deinde in textu describitur causa seu ratio horum, quæ jam evidenter expressa est : et patet textus ex dictis. Sed Moyses eadem multoties repetit, ut ea durissimis cordibus Judæorum firmius inculcaret. Quemadmodum enim lapis aut ferrum non cito recipit formam imaginis imprimendæ, sic corda illa lapidea, imo et ferrea, frequenti repetitione et incussione egebant, ut tandem divina testimonia ac mandata stabiliter retinerent : quod legislatorem eorum non latuit. Non ergo superflua fuit tam frequens repetitio.
paras.en: Next, the text sets out the cause or reason of these things, which has already been plainly stated; and the text is clear from what has been said. But Moses repeats the same things many times so as to drive them more firmly into the very hard hearts of the Jews. For as stone or iron does not quickly take the shape of an image to be stamped on it, so those hearts of stone, indeed of iron, needed frequent repetition and striking, so that at last they might hold fast the divine testimonies and commandments: and this did not escape their lawgiver. So such frequent repetition was not superfluous.

paras.t: Igitur quum emisisset Pharao populum, id est, quum fecisset Hebræos egredi de Ægypto, non eos duxit Dominus ad terram promissionis per viam terræ Philistiim, quæ vicina est Ægypto, et etiam terræ Chanaan, inter quas directe est situata, ita quod per Philistæos compendiosiori itinere de Ægypto, in terram promissionis pertingitur, et contra. Et quod via illa non sit vehementer remota et longa, inde perpenditur, quod filii Jacob ex terra promissionis in Ægyptum pro victualibus descenderunt ; tantaque inde tulerunt, quod suffecit tam in itinere quam in terra promissionis per annum aut circiter, quum tamen asini, non quadrigæ, tulerunt empta. Reputans, ne forte pœniteret eum, si videret adversum se bella consurgere, et reverteretur in Ægyptum : id est, ipse Dominus intra se cogitans, et idcirco id faciens, ne forsitan filii Israel dolerent se exisse Ægyptum, si viderent Philistæos sibi occurrere ad pugnandum. Erant equidem Philistæi duri et robustissimi bellatores. Imo Deus certe cognovit, quod in tali casu filii Israel de suo exitu pœniterent, de divino auxilio diffidentes, quemadmodum postea doluerunt, audito ab exploratoribus quales essent habitatores terræ Chanaan. Verumtamen in littera dicitur, Ne forte, non quod in divina præscientia sit aliqua incertitudo, sed ad insinuandum libertatem arbitrii, cui præcognitio nequaquam necessitatem imponit.
paras.en: [[13:17|And when Pharao had sent out the people|Igitur quum emisisset Pharao populum]], that is, when he had let the Hebrews go out of Egypt, [[13:17|the Lord led them not|non eos duxit Dominus]] to the land of promise [[13:17|by the way of the land of the Philistines|per viam terræ Philistiim]], [[13:17|which is near|quæ vicina est]] to Egypt, and also to the land of Chanaan, for it lies directly between them, so that by way of the Philistines one comes from Egypt to the land of promise, and the other way round, by a shorter route. And that this way is not very remote and long may be gathered from the fact that the sons of Jacob went down from the land of promise into Egypt for food, and brought so much from there that it sufficed both on the journey and in the land of promise for a year or thereabouts, though it was asses, not wagons, that carried what they bought. [[13:17|thinking lest perhaps they would repent, if they should see wars arise against them, and would return into Egypt|Reputans, ne forte pœniteret eum, si videret adversum se bella consurgere, et reverteretur in Ægyptum]]: that is, the Lord himself thinking within himself, and doing this for that reason, lest perhaps the children of Israel should grieve that they had left Egypt, if they saw the Philistines come out to fight them. For the Philistines were hard and most sturdy warriors. Indeed God knew for certain that in such a case the children of Israel would repent of their going out, distrusting the divine help, as they afterwards grieved when they heard from the spies what the inhabitants of the land of Chanaan were like. Yet the letter says *lest perhaps*, not because there is any uncertainty in the divine foreknowledge, but to suggest the freedom of the will, on which foreknowledge in no way imposes necessity.

paras.t: Circa hæc quidam scribit duo : Primum est, quod Philistæi erant multi et fortes bellatores, unde Josue et filii Israel non potuerunt eos debellare. Quod non videtur idonee dictum, quoniam sicut Josue et filii Israel debellaverunt Chananæos se multo fortiores, non humana, sed divina virtute, ita eadem virtute potuissent debellare et Philistæos, si Deo sic placuisset. Cur autem Deus non subjecit ipsi Josue et filiis Israel Philistæos in toto, siquidem pro parte subdidit eos illis, habetur in libro Judicum in textu, utpote ut in Philistæis experiretur Israelem, an vere timeret Dominum, et ut filii Israel haberent consuetudinem præliandi. Secundum est, Philistæi nondum demeruerunt ita puniri sicut Ægyptii, nec de terra sua expelli, sicut Chananæi. Ideo Dominus noluit quod filii Israel irent per viam terræ Philistiim. Ad quod dico, quod Philistiim erant idolatræ pessimi, quemadmodum Chananæi atque Ægyptii ; nec solum meruerunt temporaliter puniri et expelli, sed et æternaliter condemnari, quod omnem temporalem supergreditur incomparabiliter pœnam : imo Dominus promiserat filiis Israel terram Philistiim, sicut et Chananæorum. Erant enim ex genere Cham, et una decem gentium, quarum terram promiserat Israeli, ut patet in Genesi et in libris Josue ac Judicum manifeste. Quamvis autem omnipotens Deus omnia possit, non tamen vult semper omnipotentiam suam ostendere, sed secundum sapientiæ suæ censuram ac ordinem operatur.
paras.en: On these things a certain writer says two things. The first is that the Philistines were many and strong warriors, so that Josue and the children of Israel could not subdue them. This does not seem rightly said, since just as Josue and the children of Israel subdued the Chananites, who were much stronger than they, not by human but by divine power, so by the same power they could have subdued the Philistines too, had it so pleased God. But why God did not subject the Philistines wholly to Josue and the children of Israel, since he did subject them in part, is found in the text of the book of Judges: namely, that by the Philistines he might try Israel, whether it truly feared the Lord[[Judg 3:4||]], and that the children of Israel might be practised in fighting[[Judg 3:2||]] [the margin is partly lost: "Judic. […] 2, 4"; Judges 3:1–4 gives both reasons, and Judg 2:22 the first]. The second is that the Philistines had not yet deserved to be punished like the Egyptians, nor to be driven out of their land like the Chananites; therefore the Lord did not wish the children of Israel to go by the way of the land of the Philistines. To which I say that the Philistines were the worst of idolaters, as were the Chananites and the Egyptians; and they deserved not only to be punished and driven out in time, but also to be condemned eternally, which surpasses beyond compare every temporal punishment. Indeed the Lord had promised the children of Israel the land of the Philistines, as well as that of the Chananites. For they were of the race of Cham, and one of the ten nations whose land he had promised to Israel, as is plainly seen in Genesis and in the books of Josue[[Jos 13:2||]] and Judges [the margin gives Josue xiii; the land of the Philistines is named among the land still to be taken in Jos 13:2–3]. Now although almighty God can do all things, yet he does not always will to show his omnipotence, but works according to the judgement and order of his wisdom.

paras.t: Sed circumduxit filios Israel per viam deserti, quæ est juxta mare Rubrum. Nam Deus Moysi prænuntiavit, quod in montem Sinai essent venturi et ibi immolaturi. Ibi quoque voluit eis legem donare. In Ægyptiorum item demersione voluit suam demonstrare justitiam. Dicitur autem mare Rubrum, non quod aquæ sint rubræ, sed quod apparent rubræ propter fundi et lapillorum ibi jacentium ruborem, ut fertur, et quia terra in ripa est rubra, commisceturque aquæ, propter quod præcipue circa littus rubra videtur. Verumtamen in Hebræo dicitur, mare Suph, id est juncosum sive cannosum, eo quod junci sive cannæ abundent in littore. Et armati ascenderunt filii Israel de terra Ægypti. Quidam dicunt quod Ægyptii accommodaverunt Hebræis arma ad defendendum se a prædonibus, et vasa pretiosa quæ concesserant eis. Alii verisimilius dicunt, quod dicuntur ascendisse armati, quia de supellectili et pretiosis rebus Ægyptiorum eis concessis, erant bene provisi atque muniti. Quam expositionem tangit Hieronymus. Porro Septuaginta transtulerunt, Et quinta generatione ascenderunt filii Israel, etc. In Hebræo habetur, Quinta ; et pro explanatione, Septuaginta addiderunt, Generatione. Et possent generationes illæ tam in tribu Levitica, quam in tribu regia Judæ sic accipi. Nam Moyses fuit quintus a Jacob, quoniam Levi, Caath, et Amram, inter eos fuerunt. Similiter Salmon de tribu Juda qui de Ægypto egressus est, fuit quintus a Phares filio Judæ, qui cum ipso Juda intravit Ægyptum. Phares namque genuit Esron, Esron genuit Aram, Aram vero Aminadab, Aminadab vero Naasson, de quo natus est Salmon.
paras.en: [[13:18|But he led them about|Sed circumduxit]] the children of Israel [[13:18|by the way of the desert, which is by the Red Sea|per viam deserti, quæ est juxta mare Rubrum]]. For God had foretold to Moses that they would come to Mount Sinai and offer sacrifice there; there too he willed to give them the Law; and in the drowning of the Egyptians he willed to show his justice. Now it is called the Red Sea, not because its waters are red, but because they look red on account of the redness of the bottom and of the pebbles lying there, as is said, and because the earth on the shore is red and mingles with the water, so that it looks red chiefly near the shore. Yet in the Hebrew it is called the sea of Suph, that is, the sea of rushes or reeds, because rushes or reeds abound on its shore. [[13:18|and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt|Et armati ascenderunt filii Israel de terra Ægypti]]. Some say that the Egyptians lent the Hebrews arms to defend themselves against robbers, together with the precious vessels they had granted them. Others say, more probably, that they are said to have gone up armed because they were well provided and furnished with the goods and precious things of the Egyptians granted them; Jerome touches on this exposition. Further, the Septuagint translated: And in the fifth generation the children of Israel went up, etc. In the Hebrew there is *fifth*, and by way of explanation the Septuagint added *generation*. And those generations could be taken in this way both in the tribe of Levi and in the royal tribe of Juda. For Moses was the fifth from Jacob, since Levi, Caath and Amram came between them. Likewise Salmon of the tribe of Juda, who went out of Egypt, was the fifth from Phares, the son of Juda, who entered Egypt with Juda himself. For Phares begot Esron, Esron begot Aram, Aram Aminadab, Aminadab Naasson, of whom Salmon was born.

paras.t: Tulit quoque Moyses ossa Joseph secum, eo quod Joseph adjurasset filios Israel, dicens : Visitabit vos Deus, id est, gratiose liberabit posteros vestros de hac terra ; efferte ossa mea hinc vobiscum, id est, posteros vestros ad hoc obligate. Hæc autem locutus est Joseph in extremis, ut in Genesi scriptum est, ubi et verba hæc plenius exstant exposita. Circa hæc Magister in historiis scribit : Nilus tunc præter solitum adhuc inundabat terram, in qua erat sepulcrum Joseph. Tunc Moyses scripsit in lamina aurea nomen Domini tetragrammaton, quæ superposita aquæ, natavit usque dum venit et stetit super sepulcrum Joseph ; et effodientes, sustulerunt ossa ipsius, quæ sublata, leguntur eis prophetasse, forte de difficultate itineris. Tamen Hebræi tradunt, quod ovis improvise adstitit, et supernaturaliter locuta est eis. Propter quod vocabant eam ovem Joseph, et diu duxerunt eam secum per desertum, juxta illud, Qui deducis velut ovem Joseph. Porro Lyra dicit hæc esse fictitia, quia nec Josephus, nec glossæ Hebraicæ dicunt hoc. Nec verisimile est, quod ossa Joseph fuerint sepulta in campis aut pratis ubi aqua possint inundari. Circa quod dico, quod vir ille authenticus Petrus Comestor, auctor Scholasticæ historiæ, non retulisset præfata, nisi ex Hebræis et scriptis eorum hoc accepisset, vel ex aliis scriptis allegatione condignis. Denique sepulcra etiam divitum et magnatum consueverunt a Judæis fieri in hortis aut campis. Nam et Abraham, Isaac et Jacob cum suis uxoribus in spelunca duplici in agro Ephron Hethæi sepulti sunt, sicut ex Genesi patuit. Joseph quoque ab Arimathæa vir nobilis, corpus Christi sepelivit in sepulcro, quod sibi exciderat in petra sita in horto, ut patet Joannis nonodecimo ; et usque in præsens Judæi ita sepeliunt suos in pratis. Aqua autem Nili interdum tam copiose inundat, ut et loca ac monumenta alte et celebriter situata potuerit inundare. Et forte post tot annos sepulcrum Joseph fuit neglectum, aut ab Ægyptiis dehonoratum. Ideo reprobatio illa inepta est.
paras.en: [[13:19|And Moses took Joseph's bones with him|Tulit quoque Moyses ossa Joseph secum]]: [[13:19|because he had adjured the children of Israel, saying|eo quod Joseph adjurasset filios Israel, dicens]]: [[13:19|God shall visit you|Visitabit vos Deus]], that is, he will graciously set your posterity free from this land; [[13:19|carry out my bones from hence with you|efferte ossa mea hinc vobiscum]], that is, bind your posterity to this. Joseph spoke these words at the end of his life, as is written in Genesis[[Gen 50:24||]], where these words are also explained more fully. On this the Master writes in the *Histories* [Peter Comestor, *Historia scholastica*]: The Nile was then still flooding, beyond its wont, the ground where Joseph's tomb was. Then Moses wrote the Lord's four-lettered name [the Tetragrammaton] on a plate of gold, which, laid on the water, floated until it came and stood over Joseph's tomb; and digging, they took up his bones, and these, once taken up, are read to have prophesied to them, perhaps of the hardship of the journey. The Hebrews, however, relate that a sheep suddenly stood by and spoke to them in a manner above nature; for which reason they called it Joseph's sheep and long led it with them through the desert, according to that saying: [[Ps 79:2|thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep|Qui deducis velut ovem Joseph]]. Lyra, however, says that these things are made up, because neither Josephus nor the Hebrew glosses say this; nor is it likely that Joseph's bones were buried in fields or meadows where the water could flood them. To which I say that that trustworthy man, Peter Comestor, author of the *Scholastic History*, would not have related the above unless he had received it from the Hebrews and their writings, or from other writings worthy to be cited. Moreover, the tombs even of the rich and great were commonly made by the Jews in gardens or fields. For Abraham, Isaac and Jacob too were buried with their wives in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hethite, as appeared from Genesis[[Gen 23:19||]][[Gen 25:9||]][[Gen 35:27||]][[Gen 35:29||]][[Gen 49:29||]][[Gen 49:30||]][[Gen 49:31||]]. Joseph of Arimathea, too, a noble man, buried the body of Christ in a tomb [[Matt 27:60|which he had hewed out in a rock|quod sibi exciderat in petra]] set in a garden, as appears in the nineteenth of John[[John 19:41||]][[John 19:42||]]; and to this day the Jews bury their dead thus in meadows. And the water of the Nile sometimes floods so abundantly that it could flood even places and monuments set high and in frequented spots. And perhaps after so many years Joseph's tomb had been neglected, or dishonoured by the Egyptians. Therefore that objection is unfitting.

paras.t: Profectique filii Israel de Socoth, venerunt in Etham, in extremis finibus solitudinis, id est juxta terminum illius deserti ex una parte, in qua erat propinquum terræ habitabili Ægyptiorum. Unde in Scholastica fertur historia : Etham erat civitas tunc deserta in capite solitudinis, quæ a Josepho dicitur Lithus.
paras.en: [[13:20|And marching|Profectique]] the children of Israel [[13:20|from Socoth|de Socoth]] came [Denis reads *venerunt*, "came"; the margin gives the Vulgate's *castrametati sunt*, "they encamped"] [[13:20|in Etham, in the utmost coasts of the wilderness|in Etham, in extremis finibus solitudinis]], that is, near the boundary of that desert on the side where it was close to the habitable land of the Egyptians. Hence it is said in the *Scholastic History*: Etham was a city, then deserted, at the head of the wilderness, which Josephus calls Lithus.

paras.t: Dominus autem præcedebat eos ad ostendendam viam per diem in columna nubis, et per noctem in columna ignis, ut dux esset itineris utroque tempore. Columnam illam quidam dicunt fuisse unam in substantia, sed duplicem in officio, ita quod ex una parte habuit speciem ignis et lucem : et illa pars luxit Hebræis tempore noctis ut viam agnoscerent, et sibi a serpentibus præcaverent ; ex alia vero parte habuit speciem et officium nubis, quæ obumbravit Hebræos in die, ut et viam monstraret, et contra intensum solis calorem qui ibi abundat, eos protegeret. Hebræi vero (ut fertur) affirmant, quod fuit duplex columna : una nubis, in die apparens, et de vespere abiens ; alia ignis, de vespere subintrans, et mane recedens. Hanc columnam angelus movit, ideo Dominus per angelum suum ministrum dicitur eos præcessisse in columna. Quæ etsi obumbravit illos, tamen ex parte sua anteriori extendebatur in tantum, quod pro parte præcessit.
paras.en: [[13:21|And the Lord went before them to shew the way, by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire; that he might be the guide of their journey at both times|Dominus autem præcedebat eos ad ostendendam viam per diem in columna nubis, et per noctem in columna ignis, ut dux esset itineris utroque tempore]]. Some say that this pillar was one in substance but twofold in office, so that on one side it had the appearance of fire, and light, and that side gave light to the Hebrews in the night-time, so that they might see the way and guard themselves against serpents; while on the other side it had the appearance and office of a cloud, which overshadowed the Hebrews by day, both to show them the way and to protect them against the intense heat of the sun, which is great there. But the Hebrews (it is said) affirm that there were two pillars: one of cloud, appearing by day and departing in the evening; the other of fire, coming on in the evening and withdrawing in the morning. An angel moved this pillar; therefore the Lord is said to have gone before them in the pillar through his angel, his minister. And though it overshadowed them, yet with its forward part it reached out so far that in part it went before them.

13.title: De spirituali ejusdem capituli tertiidecimi intellectu
13.title_en: On the spiritual sense of the same thirteenth chapter

paras.t: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen: Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum, etc. Quemadmodum per primogenita Ægyptiorum occisa, designantur principalia vitia juste damnanda: ita per primogenita Hebræorum a morte præservata, significantur præclariores actiones virtutum, quas Dominus tempore tentationis præservat, ne vincantur a vitiis. Hæ sanctificandæ sunt Domino, id est divinæ pietati ac gratiæ humiliter adscribendæ. Nempe quum nil boni a nobismetipsis habeamus, quanto actiones virtutum fuerint in nobis eminentiores, tanto plus attribuendæ sunt Deo, ex cujus providentia oritur, ut sic vel sic ad virtutum pertingamus profectum ac verticem. Ut ergo primogenita tua consecres Deo, tanto debes esse gratior Deo atque humilior, quanto virtuosior, devotiorque exstiteris, ut cum Apostolo fatearis: Gratia Dei sum id quod sum. Ista primogenita aperiunt mentis vulvam, quia de cordis fundo ac fecunditate interna nascuntur.
paras.en: [[13:1|And the Lord spoke to Moses|Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[13:2|Sanctify unto me every firstborn|Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum]], etc. Just as the firstborn of the Egyptians that were slain signify the chief vices, which are justly to be condemned, so the firstborn of the Hebrews that were preserved from death signify the more excellent acts of the virtues, which the Lord preserves in time of temptation, lest they be overcome by the vices. These are to be sanctified to the Lord, that is, humbly ascribed to the divine goodness and grace. For since we have nothing good of ourselves, the more eminent the acts of virtue in us, the more are they to be attributed to God, from whose providence it comes that, in one way or another, we attain to progress in the virtues and to their summit. So then, that thou mayest consecrate thy firstborn to God, thou oughtest to be the more grateful to God and the humbler, the more virtuous and devout thou hast become, so as to confess with the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:10|by the grace of God, I am what I am|Gratia Dei sum id quod sum]]. These firstborn open the womb of the mind, for they are born of the depth and inward fruitfulness of the heart.

paras.t: Mementote diei hujus, in qua egressi estis de Ægypto et de domo servitutis, quoniam in manu forti eduxit vos Dominus; ut non comedatis fermentatum. Istud unicuique nostrum committitur. Egressi enim sumus de Ægypto et habitaculo servitutis, quando per veram contritionem opera tenebrarum et errores sæculi, ignorantias mentis, conversationem carnalem relinquimus; et jugiter Deo regratiari debemus, quod tamdiu nos toleravit in vita iniqua, et non solum distulit damnationis supplicia, sed insuper pro malis reddidit bona, et gratiam conversionis largitus est. Quod utique fecit in manu forti, quum majus sit peccatorem convertere, et rebellem voluntatem sine coactione salubriter immutare, quam cœlum et terram creare. Denique sæculum istud nequam recte vocatur domus miseræ servitutis, quia in eo serviunt amatores sæculi principi tenebrarum ac vitiis, et jugo subduntur iniquitatis. Propter quod princeps Apostolorum: Iniqui, inquit, sunt servi corruptionis. Et Christus: Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Cui servituti opponitur mentis sacra libertas, de qua ait Salvator: Si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis. Paulus quoque: Itaque non sumus filii ancillæ, sed liberæ, qua libertate Christus nos liberavit.
paras.en: [[13:3|Remember this day in which you came forth out of Egypt, and out of the house of bondage, for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought you forth|Mementote diei hujus, in qua egressi estis de Ægypto et de domo servitutis, quoniam in manu forti eduxit vos Dominus]]; [[13:3|that you eat no leavened bread|ut non comedatis fermentatum]]. This is committed to each one of us. For we have gone forth out of Egypt and out of the dwelling of bondage when, through true contrition, we leave behind the works of darkness and the errors of the world, the ignorances of the mind and a fleshly way of life; and we ought continually to give thanks to God that he bore with us so long in a wicked life, and not only put off the punishments of damnation, but moreover rendered good for evil and bestowed on us the grace of conversion. And this he did indeed with a strong hand, since it is a greater thing to convert a sinner, and to change a rebellious will to its salvation without compulsion, than to create heaven and earth. Lastly, this wicked world is rightly called the house of wretched bondage, because in it the lovers of the world serve the prince of darkness and the vices, and are put under the yoke of iniquity. Hence the prince of the Apostles says: The wicked are [[2 Pet 2:19|the slaves of corruption|servi corruptionis]]. And Christ: [[John 8:34|whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin|Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati]]. To this bondage is opposed the holy liberty of the mind, of which the Saviour says: [[John 8:36|If therefore the son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed|Si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis]]. Paul also: So then, [[Gal 4:31|we are not the children of the bondwoman but of the free: by the freedom wherewith Christ has made us free|non sumus filii ancillæ, sed liberæ, qua libertate Christus nos liberavit]].

paras.t: Specialiter vero religiosis incumbit, ut semper grati sint Deo, pro eo quod de mundo in maligno posito eos abstraxit, atque in claustro constituit. Nec unquam oblivisci debent diei in quo religionem ingressi sunt seu professi, ne a pristino torpescant fervore, sed juxta suæ professionis exigentiam satagant Deo digne servire, ne eis illud in Apocalypsi scriptum, a Judice summo dicatur: Habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam pristinam reliquisti. Horum itaque memores esse debemus, ne fermentatum edamus, hoc est, ne ad pristinos excessus atque errores ullatenus revertamur. Propter quod a Petro monemur: Sperate in eam, quæ vobis offertur, gratiam, non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ tenebris, sed secundum eum qui vocavit vos, et ipsi in omni conversatione sancti sitis. Rursus, domus servitutis est caro ista mortalis, quam exire debemus, passiones ejus et vitia derelinquendo, cœlestia ac spiritualia charismata cupiendo ac contemplando. Nempe ut ait Apostolus, Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt.
paras.en: But it falls especially to religious to be ever grateful to God, because he has drawn them out of the world [[1 John 5:19|seated in wickedness|in maligno posito]] and set them in the cloister. Nor ought they ever to forget the day on which they entered religion or made their profession, lest they grow cold from their first fervour; but let them strive to serve God worthily, as their profession requires, lest the words written in the Apocalypse be said to them by the supreme Judge: [[Apoc 2:4|I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam pristinam reliquisti]]. We must therefore be mindful of these things, that we eat not what is leavened, that is, that we in no way go back to our former excesses and errors. Hence we are admonished by Peter: [[1 Pet 1:13|trust perfectly in the grace which is offered you|Sperate in eam, quæ vobis offertur, gratiam]], [[1 Pet 1:14|not fashioned according to the former desires of your ignorance|non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ tenebris]] [Denis reads *tenebris*, "darkness", where the Vulgate has *desideriis*, "desires"], [[1 Pet 1:15|But according to him that hath called you|sed secundum eum qui vocavit vos]], [[1 Pet 1:15|be you also in all manner of conversation holy|et ipsi in omni conversatione sancti sitis]] [Denis leaves out *Sanctum*, "who is holy"]. Again, the house of bondage is this mortal flesh, which we must go out of by forsaking its passions and vices, and by desiring and contemplating heavenly and spiritual gifts. For, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 8:8|they who are in the flesh cannot please God|Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt]].

paras.t: Quumque introduxerit te Dominus in terram fluentem lacte et melle, id est, Christo et corpori ejus mystico, quod est Ecclesia electorum, in qua est abundantia spiritualium alimentorum, te incorporaverit, aut ad sacram religionem perduxerit, vel corpus rationi omnino subjectum tibi contulerit, celebrabis hunc morem sacrorum, id est, Pascha spiritualiter facies, et Christum in Sacramento cum vera præparatione accipies.
paras.en: [[13:5|And when the Lord shall have brought thee into|Quumque introduxerit te Dominus in]] [[13:5|a land that floweth with milk and honey|terram fluentem lacte et melle]], that is, shall have incorporated thee into Christ and into his mystical body, which is the Church of the elect, in which there is an abundance of spiritual food; or shall have brought thee to holy religion; or shall have given thee a body wholly subject to reason: [[13:5|thou shalt celebrate this manner of sacred rites|celebrabis hunc morem sacrorum]], that is, thou shalt keep the Pasch spiritually, and receive Christ in the Sacrament with true preparation.

paras.t: Primogenitum asini mutabis ove. Per asinum insensata simplicitas et hebetudo atque stoliditas denotatur: per ovem, innocentia et simplicitas bona. Itaque primogenitum asini mutamus ove, quando primordia humanæ stultitiæ et inconsiderationem propriorum periculorum abjicimus, et veram puritatem innocentiamque amplectimur. Nisi enim conversi fuerimus et effecti ut parvuli, non intrabimus regnum cœlorum. Malam ergo et asininam simplicitatem mutemus in simplicitatem columbinam, innocentiamque ovinam, ut simus prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbæ. Unde hortatur et summus Apostolus: Quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, sine dolo, lac concupiscite. Quod si non redemeris, interficies: id est, si tam perfecte te emendare nequiveris, saltem reproba confitere, et vita pristinas tuas iniquitates. Omne autem primogenitum hominis de filiis tuis, pretio redimes: id est, opera tua præcipua rationabilia, ex tuo intellectu et voluntate nascentia, virtute et merito pretiosissimi sanguinis Christi seu passionis ipsius, non propriis viribus, de manu et rabie hostium tuæ salutis, inviolata custodire conaberis.
paras.en: [[13:13|The firstborn of an ass thou shalt change for a sheep|Primogenitum asini mutabis ove]]. By the ass is denoted senseless simplicity, dullness and stupidity; by the sheep, innocence and good simplicity. So we change the firstborn of an ass for a sheep when we cast away the beginnings of human folly and heedlessness of our own dangers, and embrace true purity and innocence. For [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi enim conversi fuerimus et effecti ut parvuli, non intrabimus regnum cœlorum]] [Denis puts this in the first person: "unless we be converted and become as little children, we shall not enter"]. Let us therefore change the bad simplicity of the ass into the simplicity of the dove and the innocence of the sheep, that we may be [[Matt 10:16|wise as serpents and simple as doves|prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbæ]]. Hence the chief Apostle also exhorts us: [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile|Quasi modo geniti infantes rationabiles, sine dolo, lac concupiscite]] [Denis reads *infantes rationabiles*, "rational babes", where the Vulgate has *rationabile … lac*, "rational milk"]. [[13:13|and if thou do not redeem it, thou shalt kill it|Quod si non redemeris, interficies]]: that is, if thou canst not amend thyself so perfectly, at least confess thy reprobate deeds, and shun thy former iniquities. [[13:13|And every firstborn of men thou shalt redeem with a price|Omne autem primogenitum hominis de filiis tuis, pretio redimes]]: that is, thou shalt strive to keep thy chief rational works, born of thy intellect and will, unharmed from the hand and the fury of the enemies of thy salvation, by the power and merit of the most precious blood of Christ, that is, of his passion, not by thy own strength.

paras.t: Igitur quum emisisset Pharao populum, non eos duxit Dominus per viam terræ Philistiim, etc. Per hoc significatum est, quod Deus noviter conversos in suæ exordio conversionis frequenter custodit a gravioribus tentamentis, et pie ac dulciter tractat eos, ne victi succumbant, atque ad pristina redeant mala. Quum vero fuerint in virtutibus exercitati, spiritualibus præliis et gravioribus tentationibus eos impugnari permittit.
paras.en: [[13:17|And when Pharao had sent out the people, the Lord led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines|Igitur quum emisisset Pharao populum, non eos duxit Dominus per viam terræ Philistiim]], etc. By this it was signified that God often guards those newly converted, at the beginning of their conversion, from the heavier temptations, and treats them kindly and gently, lest they be overcome and give way, and go back to their former evils. But when they have been exercised in the virtues, he permits them to be assailed by spiritual battles and heavier temptations.

paras.t: Et armati ascenderunt filii Israel de Ægypto. Hoc impletur in nobis, quando per veram contritionem spiritualibus implemur charismatibus Spiritus Sancti, armatura virtutum, opulentia meritorum: sicque ad excelsa tendimus internorum profectuum ac evangelicæ perfectionis. Tunc Dominus nos præcedit, et viam salutis ostendit per diem, puta in prosperis, per columnam nubis, id est per refrigerationem et irrigationem supernæ illuminationis et unctionis: atque in nocte, videlicet in adversis, per columnam ignis, hoc est per terrorem divini judicii, itemque infernalis incendii, quorum consideratione in adversis patientiam observamus, nec iter virtutum relinquimus. De horum tamen significatione infra plenius disseretur.
paras.en: [[13:18|and the children of Israel went up armed|Et armati ascenderunt filii Israel]] out of Egypt. This is fulfilled in us when, through true contrition, we are filled with the spiritual gifts of the Holy Ghost, with the armour of the virtues and a wealth of merits; and so we press on towards the heights of inward progress and of evangelical perfection. Then the Lord goes before us and shows the way of salvation: by day, that is, in prosperity, by [[13:21|a pillar of a cloud|columnam nubis]], that is, by the refreshment and watering of heavenly illumination and unction; and by night, that is, in adversity, by [[13:21|a pillar of fire|columnam ignis]], that is, by the terror of the divine judgment, and likewise of the fire of hell, by the thought of which we keep patience in adversity and do not forsake the way of the virtues. But what these signify will be treated more fully below.

14.title: Expositio litteralis capituli quartidecimi: Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens: Loquere filiis Israel
14.title_en: Literal exposition of the fourteenth chapter: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel

paras.t: Capitulum istud describit, qualiter Pharao cum omni suo exercitu filios Israel persequendo penitus periit. Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens : Loquere filiis Israel, Reversi castrametentur e regione Phihahiroth : id est, hoc præcipe eis, ut paululum redeant versus Ægyptum, et castra seu tentoria sua collocent ex opposito loci, qui Phihahiroth nuncupatur, qui est inter Magdalum et mare contra Beelsephon, id est, qui locus situs est inter urbem nomine Magdalum, constitutam in Ægypti confinio, ad quam confugerunt Judæi tempore Jeremiæ prophetæ Godolia occiso, et inter locum Beelsephon dictum. In conspectu ejus castra ponetis super mare, hoc est, in loco præfato evidenter ponetis turmas vestras ac papiliones circa littus maris Rubri : quatenus Ægyptii mox venturi, putarent eos deviare a recto itinere, et esse in tali loco, quod manus suas non valerent evadere. Denique mare Rubrum in duos sinus seu per duo loca dividitur : unus sinus seu fundus est ab oriente, et Persicus appellatur, quoniam Persæ oram ejus inhabitant ; alter Arabicus dicitur.
paras.en: This chapter describes how Pharao, with all his army, perished utterly while pursuing the children of Israel. [[14:1|And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying|Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens]]: [[14:2|Speak to the children of Israel: Let them turn and encamp over against Phihahiroth|Loquere filiis Israel, Reversi castrametentur e regione Phihahiroth]]: that is, command them this, that they turn back a little toward Egypt and pitch their camp or tents opposite the place that is called Phihahiroth, [[14:2|which is between Magdal and the sea over against Beelsephon|qui est inter Magdalum et mare contra Beelsephon]]: that is, which place lies between the city named Magdal, set on the border of Egypt, to which the Jews fled in the time of the prophet Jeremias, after Godolias had been slain[[Jer 44:1||]], and the place called Beelsephon. [[14:2|you shall encamp before it upon the sea|In conspectu ejus castra ponetis super mare]], that is, in the aforesaid place you shall set your companies and pavilions in open view about the shore of the Red Sea, so that the Egyptians, who were soon to come, might think that they had strayed from the right road and were in such a place that they could not escape their hands. Further, the Red Sea is divided into two gulfs, or at two places: one gulf or basin lies to the east and is called the Persian, since the Persians dwell on its shore; the other is called the Arabian.

paras.t: Dicturusque est Pharao super filiis Israel : Coarctati sunt in terra, conclusit eos desertum : id est, Pharao cognito per exploratores et nuntios suos, quod filii Israel in loco prædicto consisterent, dicet de eis ad populum suum : Jam constituti sunt in tali loco, in terra et solitudine in qua sunt, quod evadere nequeunt ; quia (ut Josephus refert) ex una eorum parte erant asperrimi et immeabiles montes, ex alia mare Rubrum, nec patuit eis fuga, nisi per viam per quam Pharao fuit contra eos venturus. Et indurabo cor ejus, ac persequetur vos, id est, permittam eum sic indurari et excæcari, quod dolebit de hoc quod permisit vos egredi suam terram, et quasi oblitus præteritarum plagarum, insequetur vos, non attendens nec metuens potentiam atque justitiam Dei quas toties est expertus : et glorificabor in Pharaone et in omni exercitu ejus, id est, per justam ejus et suorum punitionem et submersionem, meam potentiam ac justitiam tam sublimiter declarabo, quod omnibus innotescent, et famosus ero ac gloriosus reputabor ubique. Unde supra Dominus dixit ad Pharaonem : Idcirco posui te, ut ostendam in te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra. Scientque Ægyptii quia ego sum Dominus. Pharao namque et ejus exercitus per experientiam propriæ punitionis hoc cognoverunt, et qui in Ægypto remanserant, hoc noverunt ex mirabilibus quæ Deus tunc in mari Rubro exercuit. Verumtamen Ægyptiorum cognitio, qua Dei eminentiam dominiumque noverunt, informis fuit et imperfecta, quantum ad eos qui se non emendaverunt ex ea.
paras.en: [[14:3|And Pharao will say of the children of Israel: They are straitened in the land, the desert hath shut them in|Dicturusque est Pharao super filiis Israel : Coarctati sunt in terra, conclusit eos desertum]]: that is, when Pharao has learned through his scouts and messengers that the children of Israel have halted in the aforesaid place, he will say of them to his people: Now they are set in such a place, in the land and wilderness where they are, that they cannot escape; for (as Josephus relates) on one side of them were very rugged and impassable mountains, on the other the Red Sea, and no way of flight lay open to them except by the road by which Pharao was to come against them. [[14:4|And I shall harden his heart and he will pursue you|Et indurabo cor ejus, ac persequetur vos]], that is, I will permit him to be so hardened and blinded that he will be sorry he let you leave his land, and, as though forgetting the past plagues, he will pursue you, neither heeding nor fearing the power and justice of God which he has so many times experienced: [[14:4|and I shall be glorified in Pharao, and in all his army|et glorificabor in Pharaone et in omni exercitu ejus]], that is, by the just punishment and drowning of him and his men I will show forth my power and justice so loftily that they will become known to all, and I shall be famous and reputed glorious everywhere. Hence the Lord said above to Pharao: [[Ex 9:16|therefore have I raised thee, that I may shew my power in thee, and my name may be spoken of throughout all the earth|Idcirco posui te, ut ostendam in te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra]]. [[14:4|and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord|Scientque Ægyptii quia ego sum Dominus]]. For Pharao and his army came to know this by the experience of their own punishment, and those who had stayed behind in Egypt learned it from the wonders which God then worked at the Red Sea. Yet the knowledge of the Egyptians, by which they came to know God's pre-eminence and lordship, was unformed [informis: like faith not given life by charity, a knowledge that does not change the heart] and imperfect, as regards those who did not amend themselves by it.

paras.t: Feceruntque ita. Et nuntiatum est regi Ægyptiorum quod fugisset populus. Jam ante sciebat populum Hebræorum exisse de terra sua, sed eos redituros putabat, dum expleto trium dierum itinere sacrificassent. Nunc autem percepit a nuntiis suis, qui iter et processum Israelitarum exploraverunt, quod ipsi Israelitæ non disposuerunt se ad redeundum post viam trium dierum, sed quod processerunt ulterius, ideoque proponerent omnino recedere : quod fugam esse reputaverunt Ægyptii. Immutatumque est cor Pharaonis et servorum ejus super populo, id est, propositum mutaverunt, et quos egredi compulerunt, nunc ad redeundum cogere cogitabant. Et dixerunt ad invicem: Quid volumus facere, ut dimitteremus Israel, ne serviret nobis? quasi dicant, In hoc stulte fecimus; nam et signa præhabita adscripserunt (secundum Josephum) veneficiis Moysis. Junxit ergo currum, id est, proprium suum currum jussit parari sibi, et omnem populum suum, id est quosdam de singulis, assumpsit secum. In Scholastica historia fertur: Assumpsit secum quinquaginta millia equitum, et ducenta millia peditum. Tulitque sexcentos currus electos, et quidquid in Ægypto currum fuit et duces exercitus. Secundum Josephum, accepit secum proprios currus trecentos, et totidem ab Ægyptiis. Et quod ait, Quidquid currum in Ægypto fuit, intelligendum est de electis seu elegantibus curribus, qui in bellicis solent negotiis deservire, et quos expedite quivit acquirere. Et si quæratur, qualiter habebat tot equos, patet responsio ex prædictis. Non enim omnia Ægyptiorum animalia erant grandine interfecta, sed quæ erant in agris relicta.
paras.en: [[14:4|And they did so|Feceruntque ita]]. [[14:5|And it was told the king of the Egyptians that the people was fled|Et nuntiatum est regi Ægyptiorum quod fugisset populus]]. He knew already before that the people of the Hebrews had gone out of his land, but he thought they would return when they had made their three days' journey and offered sacrifice. But now he learned from his messengers, who had spied out the route and progress of the Israelites, that the Israelites had not prepared themselves to return after the three days' journey, but had gone on further, and so meant to depart altogether: and this the Egyptians reckoned to be flight. [[14:5|and the heart of Pharao and of his servants was changed with regard to the people|Immutatumque est cor Pharaonis et servorum ejus super populo]], that is, they changed their purpose, and those whom they had driven to go out they now thought to force to return.
